# Allstate supports customers after Hurricane Isaias


Allstate helps customers file claims and navigate recovery, with additional in-person support at five mobile claims centers in Alabama and Florida


October 12, 2026


[Post](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=)


[Post](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=)


[Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=)


***UPDATE:** Mobile claims center locations are no longer being updated. The latest location information can be found*[here](https://www.allstate.com/claims/catastrophe/mobile-response-units?_ga=2.134243314.2026204665.1791838054-607167975.1791563141) *.*


**Key takeaways:**


- **File a claim anytime:** Customers can file[online](https://myaccountrwd.allstate.com/anon/account/login?returnurl=%2Fsecured%2Fclaims&_ga=2.213575639.210370550.1758575051-1512312277.1756923460) , through the[Allstate app](https://www.allstate.com/help-support/allstate-mobile?_ga=2.213575639.210370550.1758575051-1512312277.1756923460) , by calling **1-800-54-STORM (1-800-547-8676)** or by contacting an Allstate agent.
- **Get help in person:** Five[mobile claims centers](https://www.allstate.com/claims/catastrophe/mobile-response-units) in Alabama and Florida are helping customers file claims and get answers to their questions.
- **Take the next steps toward recovery:** Allstate offers guidance on documenting damage, preventing further damage and avoiding scams after the storm.


**CHICAGO, Oct. 12, 2026** — Allstate is helping customers recover from Hurricane Isaias with options to file claims anytime, in-person support at five mobile claims centers in Alabama and Florida and practical guidance.


“Allstate teams are in place to help our customers recover as quickly as possible following Hurricane Isaias,” said Mike Fiato, Executive Vice President and Chief Claims Officer at Allstate. “Whether customers need help filing a claim or understanding what comes next, we’re here to answer questions and support them through recovery.”


**How to file an Allstate claim**
Customers who experienced damage from Hurricane Isaias should file a claim as soon as it is safe to do so. Filing early helps begin the claims process and connects customers with available support resources.


Customers can file a claim 24/7 by:


- Visiting **[Allstate.com](https://myaccountrwd.allstate.com/anon/account/login?returnurl=%2Fsecured%2Fclaims&_ga=2.213575639.210370550.1758575051-1512312277.1756923460)
- Using the **[Allstate® Mobile app](https://www.allstate.com/help-support/allstate-mobile?_ga=2.213575639.210370550.1758575051-1512312277.1756923460)
- Calling **1‑800‑54‑STORM (1‑800‑547‑8676)**
- Contacting their Allstate agent
- Visiting an[Allstate mobile claims center](https://www.allstate.com/claims/catastrophe/mobile-response-units)


When it is safe, customers should document damage with photos or video, take reasonable steps to prevent additional damage and keep receipts for temporary repairs.

**Support for communities affected by Hurricane Isaias**
The Allstate Foundation supports organizations working to help communities prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters.


The Foundation donated to the American Red Cross for disaster relief and to the Center for Disaster Philanthropy to support resilience and preparedness.


**Avoiding fraud after a hurricane**
Identity theft and fraud often increase after storms and natural disasters, when scammers take advantage of disrupted routines to file false claims or pose as contractors, charities or aid workers.


Customers should be cautious of contractors who:


- Claim to be approved by FEMA or other government agencies
- Arrive unsolicited or pressure quick decisions
- Require large upfront payments or request payment in full before work begins
- Ask customers to sign contracts with blanks or exaggerate losses


Customers should verify a contractor’s credentials, obtain written estimates and carefully review contracts before signing or making a payment. Additional tips on working with a contractor are available on[Allstate’s website](https://www.allstate.com/lps/contractor) .


**Recovery resources for customers and communities**
Allstate shares recovery and safety information through the[Allstate Good Hands® Recovery Guide](https://www.allstate.com/claims/catastrophe/allstate-good-hands-recovery-guide) , available to anyone impacted by the storm.
